p.i:
'Atque adeo cunctis Cananæa tenentibus arua
Exangue trepido palpitabit cor metu.

Palpitet his certè gelida formidine pectus[?],
Inuadat horror, expauescant brachia
'Attoniti virtute tui, mutúmque stupenti
Vt dura cautes os premant silentio.

Dum populus tuus ille, tuus tibi quem ipse parasti,
O Domine, populus tutum iter pertransseat.

Hunc proprio tibi tu tecum considere monte
Vectum[?] iubebis mille per pericula,
Hic vbi stant sedes, tibi quas dudum ipse locasti,
Tuisque manibus conditum sacrarium.

Æternum Domini maneat per secula Regnum,
Æternitate sit vel ipsa longius,

Peruia qui lectà[?] genti bonus æquora fecit,
Et inter vndas tramitem siccum dedit.

At currus, & equos, peditumq;, equitumq; cateruas
Pharaonis illum persequentis obruit.

main_text.head: PARAPHRASIS IN CANTICVM MOSIS, Deuteron. xxxii. cap.

p.i:
VOs conuexi orbes nitidùm stellantis Olympi,
Atriáque, & motus animans spirabilis aër,
Quíque iubar Titan splendenti lumine vestis,

page.notes: The first verse line of the top block carries a stray mark before "Atque" that I could not identify as printed text and have left out. "pectus" is set with a ligature that is hard to read; "Vectum" and "lectà" are uncertain readings. The stanza divisions are inferred from sense and indentation. The large initial V of the last passage is transcribed as V.
